name: 九州じゃんがららあめん 秋葉原本店
address_ja: 〒101-0021 東京都千代田区外神田3-11-6
cuisine: The 1984 original of Tokyo's best-known Kyushu tonkotsu chain — six pork-bone variants plus two genuinely all-plant vegan ramen, ¥1,000–¥1,999, 18 seats, no reservations
neighborhood: Sotokanda 3-chōme — 3 min from Suehirochō (Ginza line, exit 3), 6 min from Akihabara (JR Yamanote/Keihin-Tōhoku/Sōbu and Tsukuba Express), 8 min from Akihabara (Hibiya line)
gf_detail: Not workable, including the vegan bowls. The company's own menu page states the noodle is made from 「数種類の小麦粉の配合と、卵白」 — a blend of wheat flours bound with egg white. The tonkotsu broths are pork-bone and chicken-carcass; the tsukemen tare is built on 溜まり醤油 (tamari-style soy, not declared wheat-free); 「むぎちゃん」 is explicitly a 麦味噌 (barley miso) bowl, so barley gluten as well as wheat. No allergen chart, no gluten-free claim and no wheat-free noodle appears anywhere on kyushujangara.co.jp, and the FAQ page carries no allergen section at all.
vegan_detail: Genuinely good, and the light record's 'vegan: no' was wrong. Two permanent plant-based ramen are on the Akihabara honten's own shop page: 「濃い口醤油のヴィーガンらあめん」 and 「熊本マー油のヴィーガンらあめん」. The company history is specific about how far the plant-based build goes — the 2016 shōyu bowl is described as 「スープも麺も具も植物性である初のオール・プラントベース」 (broth, noodle and toppings all plant-based) and the 2020 Kumamoto mayu bowl as 「動物性食材を一切使用せずに、豚骨のコクを思わせるスープ」. Both can be ordered 五葷抜き (no garlic/leek/chive/onion/rakkyō) for oriental-vegan diners, which the menu page spells out. What is NOT published is whether the vegan noodles are boiled in a separate pot from the tonkotsu noodles or the broth ladled with separate utensils — this is an 18-seat shop whose whole business is pork bone, so a strict vegan should ask at the counter. The group's plant-based spin-off, ヴィーガンビストロ じゃんがら in Harajuku, won the Japan Plant-Based Market Association's 日本ヴィーガンアワード2024 Restaurant/Café prize, so the plant-based work here is real rather than decorative.

chef_bio.origin: Sotokanda 3-chōme, Chiyoda-ku — this shop is the founding location
chef_bio.background: Kyushu Jangara did not start as a restaurant business. In 1979 the founder opened a cram school in Ōsaki, Shinagawa, called ブルカン塾; when recession began to squeeze the school's finances the company's own chronology says the ramen shop was opened in Sotokanda 3-chōme in 1984 as 「起死回生の策」 — a last-ditch measure to keep the school afloat. The two operations are now completely separate, but the noren and signboards still carry the ブルカン塾 name, which is the single oddest detail in Akihabara ramen. The first years were hard: the chronology records the founding trial as the belief that rich, gamey Kyushu ramen would never be accepted in Tokyo, and the answer was a deliberately milder tonkotsu — the 「九州じゃんがら」 broth, pork bone and chicken carcass balanced with several vegetables — which is still the flagship. The rest of the range was built out one broth at a time over forty years: 「ぼんしゃん」 the creamy Kurume/Hakata-rooted bowl in 1988, 「こぼんしゃん」 the Kumamoto-style mayu bowl in 1994, spice-blended 「からぼん」 and the fish-dashi tsukemen 「つけちゃん」 in 2002, barley-miso 「むぎちゃん」 in 2004. The word 「全部入り」 ("everything in") was coined at this very counter in the mid-1980s, from customers answering the staff question "what toppings?" with "put it all in!" — kakuniku pork belly descended from a Nagasaki shippoku master's recipe, mentaiko made to order by a Kyushu processor, and a whole soy-marinated soft-boiled egg served uncut. The chain has never franchised: five Tokyo shops (Akihabara, Harajuku, Ginza, Akasaka, Shibadaimon), a Bangkok partnership, and the company states plainly 「創業より今日までに上記以外の出店はございません」. Akihabara honten passed its 41st anniversary in November 2025. The founder is also a published poet-illustrator — the 元気がでる詩画集 series — and the framed illustrated letters on the shop walls are his own work.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「いい気、元気、活気、やる気」 — the company motto reflected in the 2000 brush-script logo. A milder, Tokyo-legible tonkotsu rather than a faithful Kyushu one, and since 2013 a serious parallel line of plant-based bowls rather than a token vegetarian option.
chef_bio.specialty: 「九州じゃんがら」 mild tonkotsu with 全部入り (kakuniku, mentaiko, whole ajitama); 「ぼんしゃん」 creamy tonkotsu; the two vegan ramen.

anecdotes.text: The ramen shop was opened in 1984 to rescue the founder's cram school, ブルカン塾, from recession — the school's name is still on the shop's noren and signboards.
「全部入り」, now standard ramen vocabulary, was coined at this counter when customers kept answering the topping question with "put it all in!"
In 2021 NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang used "finding Jangara ramen" as the live demo for the company's conversational-AI service at GTC21.
Tabelog lists the shop as 瓶コーク提供店 — it still serves Coke in the glass bottle.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyushujangara.co.jp carries a dated company chronology (1979 cram school, 1984 founding, every broth launch, 2013 first plant-based soup, 2016 and 2020 vegan ramen, 2024 Vegan Award), a per-shop page for Akihabara honten with address, phone, hours and the exact menu carried there, a menu page with noodle composition and the 五葷抜き option, and an FAQ that lists every shop the company has ever opened. Tabelog 13000344 confirms address 外神田3-11-6, phone 03-3251-4059, opening date 1984-11-28, 18 seats (12 counter / 6 table), no reservations, all-non-smoking, and flags ベジタリアンメニューあり.

gf_cross_contamination.text: One 18-seat kitchen whose entire output is wheat noodles. Nothing published about separate pots, and there is no wheat-free noodle to order in the first place.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The shōyu vegan bowl and the tsukemen tare are soy-sauce based with no wheat-free soy named; 「むぎちゃん」 is built on Kyushu barley miso, which is barley gluten.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The vegan bowls are formulated animal-free down to the noodle and toppings, but they are cooked in a shop whose main product is pork-bone broth, and no separate-line claim is published.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergen chart and no allergy statement anywhere on the company site, including the FAQ page.

positives.text: Menus in English, Chinese, Korean and Thai are held at every branch — ask staff. The vegan bowls are on the standard menu board, not a special order.
Cards, transport IC, PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay and UnionPay all accepted at Akihabara honten.

cultural_comfort.note: Walk-in only, no reservations, 18 seats, open 11:00–22:00 every day of the year. Multilingual menus on request, wide card and QR payment acceptance, non-smoking, child-friendly. A vegan can order off the printed menu without negotiating — point at 「ヴィーガンらあめん」 — which in a Tokyo tonkotsu shop is unusual. Expect a queue at peak; turnover is fast.

enrich_note: Confirmed in Tokyo. Coordinates moved from the neighborhood centroid to the shop's own pin. VEGAN CORRECTION: the light record had vegan_status 'no'; the shop in fact carries two permanent all-plant ramen with a 五葷抜き option, so this is raised to 'options'. GF stays 'no' — the noodle is wheat flour bound with egg white by the company's own description.

name: 麺処 マゼル（MAZERU）
address_ja: 〒101-0025 東京都千代田区神田佐久間町1-14 第2東ビル 1F
cuisine: Seven-seat Jirō-style mazesoba counter 68 m from Akihabara station — soy or salt, 200/300/400 g of very thick flat noodle, ¥900–¥1,350, free garlic/veg/fat/extra-tare/cheese calls, cash only
neighborhood: Kanda-Sakumachō 1-chōme — 1 min from Akihabara (JR Yamanote/Keihin-Tōhoku/Sōbu, Hibiya line, Tsukuba Express), 4 min from Iwamotochō (Toei Shinjuku line)
gf_detail: Wheat from end to end. Jirō-lineage mazesoba is a very thick flat wheat noodle — reviewers describe it as 「二郎系の中でかなり太目の平打ち」 — dressed with a soy-sauce tare; the table condiments include a しょうゆダレ bottle. Pork chāshū braised in soy. No allergen information is published and the shop has no website or listed phone number.
vegan_detail: Pork chāshū and pork fat (アブラ) are the point of the dish; the tare is soy-sauce based and the shop's only non-meat call is extra cabbage/beansprouts on top of a pork bowl. Nothing plant-based is offered.

roles: 店主 (owner-cook) plus one or two assistants
chef_bio.background: Mazeru opened on 21 February 2011 in the ground floor of the Dai-2 Higashi Building, sixty-eight metres from the Akihabara ticket gates, and has run as a seven-seat counter ever since — no phone number published, no website, no reservations, cash only, one owner-cook working with an assistant or two. It is a Jirō-descended mazesoba specialist rather than a ramen shop: no soup, a mound of very thick flat straight noodle in 200 g / 300 g / 400 g weights, soy or salt tare, and the free topping calls that come with the lineage — ニンニク (garlic), ヤサイ (cabbage and beansprouts, roughly 8:2, boiled to stay crunchy), アブラ (back fat), 味濃いめ/カラメ (extra tare) — plus cheese, which is Mazeru's own addition and the one that regulars order. Two thick slices of well-braised pork come as standard, with a 肉増し option. Chopsticks only, no soup spoon; black pepper, ichimi and a soy-tare bottle on the counter; anime songs on the stereo and a young, quiet, wordless service style. Prices run ¥900 for a regular shōyu bowl to ¥1,350 for a 400 g salt bowl with extra pork, which is why Tabelog's own budget band for the shop sits under ¥999.
chef_bio.philosophy: Jirō-lineage mazesoba at a station-adjacent seven-seat counter: one dish, two tares, three noodle weights, free calls, no talk.
chef_bio.specialty: まぜそば (shōyu or shio), 200/300/400 g; cheese as a topping call; 肉増し for extra pork.

anecdotes.text: Seven seats, all counter, no published telephone number, cash only — Tabelog lists 予約可否 as 予約不可 and お問い合わせ as 非公開.
Cheese is a standard free-call topping alongside the usual Jirō garlic/veg/fat, and reviewers say it turns the non-emulsified tare milky.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13122931 gives the address 神田佐久間町1-14 第2東ビル1F, opening date 2011-02-21, 7 counter seats, hours 11:30–15:00 / 17:30–21:00 Mon–Sat with Sun/holidays closed, cash only, all-non-smoking, and 秋葉原駅から68m. A Jirō-lineage review site (ramen-jiro-pc3.com) itemises the full price list, the noodle weights, the topping calls and the counter condiments.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A one-pot, seven-seat noodle counter. Everything served passes through the same wheat-noodle water.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Shōyu tare, soy-braised pork, and a soy-tare bottle on the counter. No wheat-free soy named.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No website, no published phone, no allergen information of any kind.

cultural_comfort.note: Seven counter seats, cash only, no English menu published, and the ordering ritual is the Jirō one — you are asked for your topping calls as the bowl is assembled and you are expected to answer fast. Portions start large: 200 g of noodle is the small. Fine to enter alone; Tabelog flags it as 一人で入りやすい. Closed Sundays and public holidays.

enrich_note: Confirmed in Tokyo at 神田佐久間町1-14; coordinates moved from the neighborhood centroid to the shop pin. GF/vegan both stay 'no'. Chef bio confidence is 'medium' rather than 'high' because the shop publishes nothing itself — the owner is not named anywhere I could find, and the operational detail comes from Tabelog's shop record plus one specialist review site.

name: 昭和食堂 秋葉原駅前店
address_ja: 〒101-0021 東京都千代田区外神田1-15-11 秋葉原西川ビル 1F
cuisine: A 25-seat counter 110 m from the Electric Town exit selling one thing loudly — 名物スタミナ丼, pork and spring onion in garlic soy over rice with a raw egg and miso soup, ¥980 for regular OR large, up to a 1 kg ギガ盛 at ¥2,980
neighborhood: Sotokanda 1-chōme, 110 m from the Akihabara Electric Town exit (JR Yamanote/Keihin-Tōhoku/Sōbu); Hibiya line and Tsukuba Express Akihabara are both a few minutes further
gf_detail: The house dish is defined by wheat soy sauce: Tabelog's own menu text for 名物スタミナ丼 reads 「豚肉&ネギにニンニク醤油でスタミナ満点！生卵、味噌汁付」 — pork and spring onion in garlic-soy, with raw egg and miso soup. Every donburi and teishoku comes with that miso soup; the teishoku list runs to karaage and shōgayaki, both wheat-coated or soy-marinated. No allergen information is published anywhere and the shop has no website. The light record's 'gf: ask' overstated it.
vegan_detail: Pork in the two flagship bowls, a raw egg on top of one of them, offal in the ホルモン丼, dashi in the miso soup that comes with everything. There is no vegetable dish on the menu that is not a garnish. The light record's 'vegan: limited' was not supportable.

chef_bio.background: This is not the Nagoya izakaya chain of the same name — that 昭和食堂 belongs to 株式会社海帆 and is a different business entirely. The Akihabara 昭和食堂 is one shop, opened 26 April 2010 in the Akihabara Nishikawa Building a hundred metres from the station's Electric Town exit, a 25-seat counter with a corrugated-iron patch on the front wall and a ticket machine inside the door. It exists to serve スタミナ丼: pork and spring onion cooked hard in garlic soy, piled on rice, raw egg on top, miso soup alongside. The pricing is the gimmick and the appeal — 並盛 and 大盛 are the same ¥980, メガ盛 is double the regular at ¥1,780 and ギガ盛 is double that again at ¥2,980, which lands somewhere near a kilo. The house line on how to eat it is to start with lemon and pepper for a lighter version, switch to the special tare for a heavier one, then break the egg in partway through so it eats as two dishes. 豚キムチ丼 runs the same four-size ladder at the same prices; まかない丼 and ホルモン丼 fill out the board, with karaage and shōgayaki teishoku for anyone who wants a plate instead of a bowl. Takeaway is available and the shop takes cards and most e-money, which for a ¥980 stamina bowl is generous. Tabelog notes drily that the toilet is downstairs and shared with the tsukemen shop やすべえ.
chef_bio.philosophy: Volume at a flat price. Large costs the same as regular; if you want more than that, the menu keeps doubling.
chef_bio.specialty: 名物スタミナ丼 (並/大 ¥980, メガ ¥1,780, ギガ ¥2,980), 豚キムチ丼, ホルモン丼.

anecdotes.text: 並盛 and 大盛 are priced identically at ¥980 — the ticket machine offers four sizes on one screen and the first two cost the same.
The restroom is downstairs and shared with the tsukemen shop やすべえ in the same building.
The shop's own suggested method: lemon and pepper for the light version, the special tare for the heavy one, then mix the raw egg in halfway so it tastes like two dishes.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13109860 gives the address 外神田1-15-11 秋葉原西川ビル1F, phone 03-6206-9721, opening date 2010-04-26, 25 counter seats, 11:00–23:00 daily with no closing day, all-non-smoking, takeaway, cards and e-money accepted, plus the shop's own PR copy and a full priced menu updated 2026-01-01. A 2025 Akihabara food blog (umalog.jp) photographs the ticket machine and confirms the four-size ladder in person.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Karaage is fried in the same small kitchen that plates every other order; no separate-fryer claim exists.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: ニンニク醤油 is the defining seasoning of the house dish, and miso soup comes with every bowl and set. No wheat-free soy or miso is named.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No website, no allergen chart, no published allergy policy. Ordering is by ticket machine, so there is no natural point at which to raise a dietary question before the food is cooked.

positives.text: Cards (VISA/JCB/AMEX/Diners) and transport IC, Edy, iD and QUICPay are accepted, which is unusual at this price point.

cultural_comfort.note: Ticket machine at the door, counter seating, open 11:00–23:00 every day, 110 m from the station. No English menu is published but the ticket machine is picture-driven and the choice is essentially one dish in four sizes. Order 並盛 unless you have seen the photographs — メガ盛 is twice that and ギガ盛 is four times.

enrich_note: Confirmed in Tokyo; coordinates moved to the shop pin. DISAMBIGUATION: this is a single independent Akihabara shop, not the Nagoya izakaya chain 昭和食堂 operated by 株式会社海帆 — same name, unrelated business. GF and vegan both downgraded from the light record's 'ask'/'limited' to 'no': the signature dish is pork in garlic soy with a raw egg, and miso soup comes with everything.

name: 新田毎（しんたごと）
address_ja: 〒101-0021 東京都千代田区外神田1-17-6 JR秋葉原駅 中央・総武緩行線 千葉方面6番ホーム（改札内）
cuisine: A 1968 standing-soba counter inside the ticket gates on Akihabara's platform 6 — もりそば ¥400, big kakiage and tempura soba ¥570–¥600, and a genuinely famous ステーキカレー; open 06:30–23:00, 365 days
neighborhood: Inside JR Akihabara station, on the Chūō-Sōbu local line Chiba-bound platform (no. 6) — the top level of the station; you need a valid ticket or IC touch-in to reach it
gf_detail: A station standing-soba counter is close to the worst case in Japan. The tsuyu is wheat soy sauce, the noodle is a blended soba (the shop sells 生そば alongside udon from the same pot of water), and the counter's whole trade is dropping pre-fried tempura — squid, three-vegetable, shungiku, chicken — into bowls. There is a curry line as well, and Japanese restaurant curry roux is wheat flour by default. No allergen information exists. The light record's 'gf: ask' was too generous.
vegan_detail: The tsuyu is a bonito-forward station dashi, tempura batter at this kind of counter is normally egg-bound, the curry is beef/steak, and udon shares the noodle water with soba. Nothing on the eighteen-item board is animal-free. The light record's 'vegan: limited' was not supportable.

roles: operated by メトロ商事 (Metro Shōji)
chef_bio.background: Shintagoto has stood on the Chiba-bound Sōbu line platform at Akihabara since 1968 — the year of the Tokyo University riots and the ¥300 million robbery, as one soba chronicler cheerfully points out. It is run by メトロ商事, which also owns the Yūrakuchō curry restaurant ふくてい, and that sibling relationship explains the shop's actual claim to fame: the ステーキカレー, whose signboard is visible from passing trains and which is far better than a platform curry counter has any business being. The soba side is honest cheap station work — もりそば ¥400 with nothing but spring onion and wasabi, いか天そば ¥600 with two large soft squid tempura, 三種野菜天そば ¥580 with shredded burdock, carrot and komatsuna, and a 春菊天そば ¥570 whose chrysanthemum-leaf fritter is notorious for arriving the size of an entire supermarket pack and hanging over the rim of the bowl. Twenty standing places, non-smoking, ticket machine, cash or transport IC. The other local institution is the time service: discounts and free add-ons appear in waves through the day rather than at one fixed hour, and the shop's own Tabelog copy boasts about it — half price on some items, free extras on others, on top of prices that were already low. Open from half past six in the morning to eleven at night, every day of the year, which for a commuter changing at Akihabara is the entire point.
chef_bio.philosophy: Station soba as a public utility: open before the first rush and after the last, cheap, fast, standing, and with a curry good enough to be a destination.
chef_bio.specialty: ステーキカレー; 春菊天そば (oversized shungiku fritter); とり天そば; もりそば ¥400.

anecdotes.text: The shop is a sibling of the Yūrakuchō curry restaurant ふくてい under the same operator, メトロ商事 — which is why the steak curry on a station platform is the item people travel for.
Founded in 1968 and still on the same platform.
The shungiku tempura is described as looking like an entire supermarket pack of chrysanthemum greens fried whole, spilling over the edge of an already large bowl.
Tabelog's shop PR is mostly about the rolling time-service discounts: 「ラッキーだと思っていたタイムサービスが時間の経過と共に次々登場する」.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13058670 gives the address as 外神田1-17-6 JR秋葉原駅 総武線6番ホーム, phone 03-3255-4983, 06:30–23:00, 20 standing counter places, non-smoking, cash and transport IC only, takeaway available, and access as 「JR「秋葉原駅」改札内」. A dedicated Chiyoda soba menu site itemises eighteen dishes with prices and ingredients; a 2026 standing-soba blog adds the 1968 founding date and the メトロ商事 / ふくてい relationship.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Soba and udon are boiled in the same water at a standing counter, and pre-fried tempura is dropped straight into bowls. Nothing is segregated.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Station tsuyu is wheat soy sauce and the shop names no alternative. The curry roux is a further wheat source.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Bonito dashi tsuyu; beef in the flagship curry; shared noodle water.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Ticket-machine ordering at a standing counter with a three-minute service cycle. There is no realistic opportunity to discuss ingredients, and no allergen chart is published.

cultural_comfort.note: Two practical warnings. First, it is INSIDE the ticket gates on platform 6 — you cannot walk in from the street, you need a ticket or an IC touch-in, and platform 6 is the topmost level of Akihabara station. Second, it is standing-only, cash or transport IC, ticket machine, Japanese-only board, and the whole transaction is expected to take about four minutes. Wonderful if you are changing trains; not a sit-down meal.

enrich_note: Confirmed in Tokyo, still trading (Tabelog reviews through 2026/08). Coordinates moved to the platform pin. ACCESS FLAG: the shop is inside the JR ticket gates on platform 6 and is not reachable without a valid ticket — worth surfacing in the app, since the map pin sits on a street address the diner cannot use. GF downgraded 'ask'→'no' and vegan 'limited'→'no'.

name: ごはん処 あだち
address_ja: 〒101-0021 東京都千代田区外神田3-11-6
cuisine: Akihabara's legendary big-portion teishoku shop — home-style fried chicken, croquette, thick omelette and nimono on one tray, and a rice bowl whose 'regular' is a shō (about 3.5 kg); ¥1,000–¥1,999
neighborhood: Sotokanda 3-chōme, in the same small building as Kyushu Jangara honten — 3 min from Akihabara (JR), a couple of minutes from Suehirochō (Ginza line)
gf_detail: The signature tray is built on wheat: crumbed korokke, karaage in a thick crunchy coating, tempura, and nimono in soy-based broth, with miso soup alongside. No allergen information exists, the shop has no website, and the kitchen is one fryer serving everything. The light record's 'gf: ask' overstated it.
vegan_detail: Chicken karaage, thick rolled omelette, croquette and soy-simmered nimono are the standing plate; the miso soup will be bonito dashi. No plant-based dish or accommodation is published. The light record's 'vegan: limited' was not supportable.

roles: 大将 (owner-cook) working the counter himself
chef_bio.background: Adachi is an eighteen-seat teishoku shop in a back lane behind Akihabara — six counter places and six two-tops — that has become the city's best-known big-portion pilgrimage, described in Japanese food writing as 「都内デカ盛りの聖地（ラスボス）」, the last boss. The food itself is unremarkable in the best sense: a child's-fist-sized piece of fried chicken, a croquette, thick tamagoyaki, a piece of tempura, a bowl of nimono, all in the register one blogger calls 「実家を思い出すようなホッとする美味しさ」. What makes it famous is the rice. The house 普通盛り is a shō — around 3.5 kg, roughly twenty rice bowls — and is not a joke portion but the default, which is why the shop has evolved a private vocabulary for asking for less: 「擦り切れ」 (level with the rim of the bowl, about 600 g, still more than a large elsewhere) and 「11軽」 for less again. Regulars say the essential thing is that the owner is kind about it — he asks 「食べられる？無理しないでね」 before he serves, and applauds when the tray comes back clean, because the one thing the shop does not want is waste. It is cash only, all-smoking, 不定休 with no fixed rest day, and its evening service runs to 23:30 on weekdays while weekends are lunch only. Reservations are accepted by phone, which for a counter this size is unusual and worth using.
chef_bio.philosophy: Home cooking at a scale that has become a challenge by accident. Order the size you can finish; the owner would rather you asked for less than left food.
chef_bio.specialty: あだちランチセット — karaage, croquette, tamagoyaki, tempura, nimono, miso soup and as much rice as you dare call for.

anecdotes.text: The default 普通盛り of rice is one shō — about 3.5 kg, roughly twenty bowls. First-timers are told to say 「擦り切れ」 (~600 g) or 「11軽」 instead.
The owner asks whether you can finish before he serves and tells you not to push it; the shop's real rule is no food waste.
It shares a building address — 外神田3-11-6 — with Kyushu Jangara's 1984 flagship, so two of Akihabara's best-known eating institutions sit on the same tiny footprint.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13024210 gives the address 外神田3-11-6, phone 03-3253-3017, 18 seats (6 counter + six two-tops), reservations accepted, 11:30–15:00 and 17:00–23:30 weekdays with weekends lunch only, 不定休, cash only, all-smoking. A 2026 big-portion blog documents the rice sizing vocabulary, the tray contents and the owner's handling of first-timers in person.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Karaage, croquette and tempura all come off the same fryer onto the same tray. No separation of any kind is claimed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Nimono is soy-simmered and miso soup comes with the set; no wheat-free soy or miso is named.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No website and no allergen information. The owner does talk to every customer about portion size before serving, so a question would at least be heard — but it would have to be asked in Japanese.

cultural_comfort.note: Cash only, no English menu, and — importantly for anyone sensitive — Tabelog records the shop as 全席喫煙可, smoking permitted throughout, which is now rare in Tokyo. Eighteen seats, phone reservations accepted (03-3253-3017), no fixed closing day so check before travelling. Weekends are lunch only. If you go, know the rice vocabulary before you sit down: say 「擦り切れで」 unless you have specifically come for the challenge.

enrich_note: Confirmed in Tokyo at 外神田3-11-6; coordinates moved to the shop pin. GF downgraded 'ask'→'no' and vegan 'limited'→'no' — the tray is fried food and soy-simmered nimono with miso soup. HUMAN FLAG: the shop is all-smoking indoors, which may matter more to some users than the cuisine.

name: 天ぷら ひさご 秋葉原店
address_ja: 〒101-0021 東京都千代田区外神田4-14-1 秋葉原UDX（AKIBA-ICHI）3F
cuisine: Edomae tempura from a house founded in Hibiya in 1918 — counter service with each piece fried to order in premium sesame oil, tendon from ¥1,200 at lunch and eight-piece courses from ¥5,300; 38 seats with private rooms
neighborhood: Sotokanda 4-chōme, third floor of the Akihabara UDX building — 3 min from Akihabara (JR Yamanote/Keihin-Tōhoku/Sōbu, Hibiya line, Electric Town exit), 4–5 min from Suehirochō (Ginza line)
hours_raw: ランチ 11:00～15:00／ディナー 17:00～22:00（L.O. 21:00）　定休日：不定休（秋葉原UDXに準ずる）　※2025年12月27日より改装のため休業中、2026年10月末（予定）まで
gf_detail: A tempura specialist: every dish that leaves the kitchen is wheat batter in a shared oil bath, and the tendon tare is a soy-and-mirin reduction. The shop's own こだわり page is about the sesame oil (special order from 磯村政次郎商店, made by 九鬼産業) and the thinness of the batter, not about allergens; no allergen chart or gluten-free claim appears on the site, the gnavi listing or Tabelog.
vegan_detail: There is a real vegetable-only headline item — 野菜天丼 ¥1,200, weekdays only, listed among the shop's three recommended dishes — and Tabelog flags the shop as 野菜料理にこだわる / ベジタリアンメニューあり. But nothing published says the batter is egg-free (Edomae tempura batter normally is not) or that the tendon tare is free of dashi and mirin, and the same oil fries anago and kisu all service. A vegetarian will eat well here; a strict vegan should treat this as an 'ask at booking' rather than a yes.

roles: 職人 (counter tempura chefs); the owner personally selects the sake list
chef_bio.origin: Founded 1918 (大正7年) in Hibiya; the Akihabara branch opened 2006
chef_bio.background: Hisago's own copy dates the house to 大正7年 — 1918 — when it opened in Hibiya, later moving to Yūrakuchō and then Hirakawachō, where it traded as a ryōtei. It now runs four branches: Akihabara, Ginza, Nagoya and Hakata. The Akihabara room opened in 2006 on the third floor of the UDX complex and is the least old-fashioned expression of the house — a bright, modern, wheelchair-accessible dining room of 38 seats with eleven at the counter, a genuinely private four-to-six-seat room and a partitioned space that takes up to 22 for a party. The kitchen's two published obsessions are the oil and the batter. The oil is a special-order top-grade sesame oil sold by 磯村政次郎商店 of Kotobuki, Taitō-ku and pressed by 九鬼産業 in Yokkaichi, chosen because it fries golden and, in the shop's words, 「決してもたれません」 — never sits heavily. The batter is deliberately thin so the ingredient stays visible, which the shop says is what makes its kakiage — its self-declared hardest and proudest item — work. Fish is bought at Toyosu and the anago and kisu are filleted in-house; the rice is Akita Komachi 「幸せこまち」 from Ōgata village, grown on minimal agrochemicals and natural organic phosphate fertiliser. Prices sit deliberately between a lunch counter and a formal tempura-ya: tendon ¥1,200, tempura teishoku ¥1,500, the signature ひさご天丼 ¥1,650, ひさご天ぷら定食 ¥2,300, a large prawn tendon ¥2,980, and 特選天ぷらコース from ¥5,300 for eight pieces, with a two-person pair set at ¥6,600. Menus are held in English and Korean and at least some counter staff work in English, which for an Edomae tempura counter is unusual.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「創業百年超・江戸前天ぷら一筋」 — a century on one dish. Premium sesame oil, thin batter so the ingredient shows, and Edomae technique at a price an office worker can meet at lunch.
chef_bio.specialty: かき揚げ; 穴子の一本揚げ ¥1,320; ひさご天丼 ¥1,650; 特選天ぷらコース from ¥5,300; 野菜天丼 ¥1,200 (weekdays).

anecdotes.text: The house dates itself to 1918 in Hibiya, later trading as a ryōtei in Hirakawachō before becoming a tempura specialist with branches in Akihabara, Ginza, Nagoya and Hakata.
The sesame oil is named on the wall: sold by 磯村政次郎商店 (Taitō-ku, in business ~70 years), pressed by 九鬼産業 (Yokkaichi, ~128 years).
The rice is 'Shiawase Komachi' Akita Komachi from Ōgata village, grown with minimal agrochemicals so that wildlife can coexist with the paddies.
The dining room is wheelchair-accessible including the toilet, and the gnavi listing records English and Korean menus with English-speaking staff.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: hisagoakihabara.com (the shop's own site) gives the address, hours, phone 03-3252-3051, the sesame-oil and rice sourcing, the kakiage technique note, seat and private-room counts and the lunch/course price bands. The shop's gnavi page adds the 1918 Hibiya founding, the four-branch structure, the 'over 100 years of tempura only' tagline, the coordinates 35.7007371/139.7726036, the accessibility and language provisions, and — critically — the current notice 「2025年12月27日より当面の間休業となります」. Tabelog 13021930 independently states 「改装のため、2026年１０月末（予定）まで休業しております」.

gf_cross_contamination.text: One oil bath, wheat batter on every item, all service long. There is no gluten-free path through a tempura counter.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Tendon tare is a soy-and-mirin reduction; no wheat-free soy is named anywhere on the shop's site or listings.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The weekday 野菜天丼 is vegetable tempura, but it is fried in the same oil as anago and kisu, and neither the batter's egg content nor the tare's dashi content is published.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergen chart published. However the shop takes reservations by phone and online, holds English and Korean menus and has English-speaking staff, so a dietary request can be made before you arrive.

positives.text: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and toilet, private rooms, free Wi-Fi, all-non-smoking, and full card/PayPay acceptance.

cultural_comfort.note: CLOSED FOR RENOVATION as of writing — the shop's own gnavi page carries 「2025年12月27日より当面の間休業となります」 and Tabelog states the closure runs to end of October 2026 (planned). Check before travelling. When open it is one of the more approachable tempura counters in central Tokyo: English and Korean menus, some English-speaking staff, cards and PayPay, private rooms, step-free access, and a ¥1,200 weekday tendon that lets you eat serious Edomae tempura for the price of a chain lunch.

The light record read 「天ぷら白子（Tempura Hisago）」. 白子 reads shirako, not hisago; the business at that pin is 天ぷら ひさご 秋葉原店 (ひさご = 瓢), Sotokanda 4-14-1, UDX 3F, with its own site at hisagoakihabara.com — the romanisation in the light record was right and the kanji was a garbling. It should be suppressed or badged in the app until that date is confirmed. Vegan raised 'no'→'ask' on the strength of a permanent weekday 野菜天丼 and the shop's ベジタリアンメニューあり flag, with the batter/tare caveats spelled out.

name: 神田まつや 本店
address_ja: 〒101-0041 東京都千代田区神田須田町1-13
cuisine: Tokyo's most-loved surviving Edo soba house, founded 1884 and trading in a wooden building the city has listed — もり/かけ ¥825, ざる ¥1,045, and the famous grilled chicken skewers to drink with; no reservations, cash only
neighborhood: Kanda-Sudachō 1-chōme — 2 min from Awajichō (Marunouchi line), 3 min from Ogawamachi (Toei Shinjuku line), 4 min from Kanda (Ginza line), 7 min from Kanda (JR Chūō line)
gf_detail: Not workable, and unusually well evidenced for a soba house. Matsuya's own shop description states the dough is 「外2割でつなぎに小麦粉を加え」 — soto-nihachi, wheat flour added as the binder at 20% on top of the buckwheat — and that the water is 卵水, egg water, adjusted by weather and kneading time. On top of that the tsuyu is wheat soy sauce (cold soba dressed with honbushi and sōda-bushi, hot with saba-bushi), the menu runs to tempura soba, tendon and tempura gohan, and udon shares the kitchen. There is no jūwari option. The light record's 'gf: ask' should be read as 'no'.
vegan_detail: Egg is in the noodle dough itself (卵水), before you reach the bonito/mackerel dashi in every tsuyu, the egg-bound dishes that make up half the menu (玉子とじ, 月見, かき玉, 親子丼, 玉子丼) and the chicken nanban. 花巻 (nori) and 山かけ (grated yam) look plant-based on paper but sit in the same wheat-soy bonito tsuyu. There is no vegan path here.

roles: 小高家 (the Odaka family) — owner-proprietors since the Meiji era
chef_bio.background: Matsuya opened in 1884 (明治17年) and has been carried by the Odaka family ever since. The building it trades in is the reason people photograph the street: a wooden merchant's house of the interwar years, designated a 東京都選定歴史的建造物 — a Tokyo Metropolitan Government Selected Historic Building — in 2001, so the low ceiling, the long shared tables and the lattice front are legally protected rather than a pastiche. The soba is stone-milled to order: buckwheat bought from Ibaraki and Hokkaidō, selected by grain and milled on the shop's specified stones, then cut soto-nihachi with wheat flour as the binder and egg water whose quantity the cutters change according to the day's weather and how long the dough has been worked — the shop's stated aim being koshi and throat-feel rather than aroma alone. The dashi is split by temperature: honbushi and sōda-bushi for cold soba, saba-bushi for hot. What separates Matsuya from other historic soba houses is the drinking culture. It is a lunch counter and an evening tavern at once; the yakitori is a house speciality and the room at four in the afternoon is largely people with a bottle of sake, a plate of grilled chicken and a seiro to finish, which is the older Edo way of using a soba shop and now survives in very few places. Ikenami Shōtarō wrote about it and the association has stuck. Tabelog has picked it for the そば百名店 list in both 2021 and 2024. Sixty-six seats at shared tables, no reservations, no cards or e-money at all, closed Sundays and Mondays.
chef_bio.philosophy: Keep the Meiji-era house and the Meiji-era way of using it — soba to finish a drink, not soba as a ceremony. Stone-milled buckwheat, soto-nihachi, dashi changed by temperature, prices an office worker can pay every week.
chef_bio.specialty: もり／かけ ¥825, ざるそば ¥1,045, くるみそば, 花巻, そばとろ, かしわ南ばん; 焼き鳥 to drink with; seasonal ひやむぎ in high summer and 節句そば「くさきり」.

anecdotes.text: The building was designated a Tokyo Metropolitan Government Selected Historic Building in 2001 and the shop still trades in it.
The dough is soto-nihachi — 20% wheat flour added as binder — kneaded with 卵水, egg water, whose amount is changed according to the weather and the working time.
Cold soba is dressed with honbushi and sōda-bushi, hot soba with saba-bushi: two different dashi under one roof.
Selected for Tabelog's そば百名店 in both 2021 and 2024, with over 3,100 reviews and 120,000 saves — one of the most-recorded soba shops in Japan.
The shop's own site announces seasonal specials in the old way — a くさきり soba for the seasonal festival, and a summer ひやむぎ — and it still sends soba by post from the same page.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kanda-matsuya.jp is the shop's own (Shift-JIS, frameset-era) site: it carries the honten menu with prices as revised 2024-11-26, the mail-order page, the access map and the proprietor's seasonal notices signed 神田まつや本店. Tabelog 13000340 gives the address 神田須田町1-13, phone 03-3251-1556, the 1884 opening date, 66 table seats, no reservations, cash only, all-non-smoking, the two そば百名店 selections, the historic-building designation, and the shop PR text containing the soto-nihachi and egg-water statements.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Wheat is inside the noodle, not merely nearby: soto-nihachi with wheat flour as the binder, plus dusting flour, plus udon in the same kitchen and tempura on the menu.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard wheat soy sauce in both the cold and hot tsuyu; no tamari or wheat-free alternative named.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Egg water in the dough itself, and bonito/sōda/saba dashi in every tsuyu. Even the plainest bowl fails on both counts.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergen information is published. The shop takes no reservations, so there is no pre-arrival channel to raise a dietary need.

positives.text: The shop is unusually explicit in print about what is in its dough, which is itself useful — most soba houses say nothing at all.

cultural_comfort.note: CASH ONLY — no cards, no e-money, no QR. No reservations; you queue, and at lunch the queue is long even after 13:00, though the room turns over fast. Sixty-six seats at shared tables, so expect to be sat with strangers, which is normal and part of the experience. Closed Sundays AND Mondays. Non-smoking. Prices are modest (¥825–¥1,540 for almost everything). No English menu is published, but the board is short and 「もり」 or 「ざる」 will get you the shop's best dish.

enrich_note: Confirmed in Tokyo; coordinates moved from the neighborhood centroid to the shop pin at 神田須田町1-13. GF downgraded 'ask'→'no' and vegan 'limited'→'no' on the shop's own published statement that the dough is soto-nihachi with wheat-flour binder kneaded with egg water — a rare case where a soba house documents exactly why it cannot serve a celiac or a vegan, and the record should say so plainly.

address_ja: 〒101-0062 東京都千代田区神田駿河台2-6-1 御茶ノ水山水ビル 1F — PERMANENTLY CLOSED, address recorded for the audit trail only
cuisine: CLOSED — was a standing-soba counter a minute inside the Ochanomizu-bashi exit; the house bowl 「明神そば」 at ¥500 came loaded with meat, tenkasu, abura-age, wakame and a boiled egg, against ¥280 for plain kake
neighborhood: Was Kanda-Surugadai 2-chōme, under a minute from the JR Ochanomizu Ochanomizu-bashi gate
hours_raw: （閉店）最終営業時の掲載：月〜金 06:30 - 14:00、土日祝 定休。それ以前は 6:30〜20:00（土曜15時まで）
gf_detail: Not assessed for a live listing — the business is gone. For the record, it was a standing-soba counter: wheat soy tsuyu, tenkasu (fried wheat batter) as a standard topping, blended soba. Nothing about it would have been gluten-free.
vegan_detail: Not assessed for a live listing. The house bowl carried meat and a boiled egg, and a reviewer specifically notes the tsuyu was strongly bonito-forward — 「出汁（カツオ節）感が強く」.

chef_bio.background: Myōjin Soba was the standing-soba counter immediately inside the Ochanomizu-bashi exit at Ochanomizu station, in the ground floor of the Ochanomizu Sansui Building, with a door on each side and a ticket machine at each door so that a commuter with a train to catch could start from whichever side he arrived on. Its name bowl, 「明神そば」 at ¥500, was effectively an everything-on: sliced meat, tenkasu, abura-age, wakame and a boiled egg over soba, against ¥280 for a plain kake — which is why local writers called it the best five-hundred-yen meal at the station. It closed on 20 July 2020, and a Tabelog reviewer records that the loss of Myōjin Soba together with the closure of そば新 at the Hijiribashi exit wiped standing-soba culture out of Ochanomizu in a single summer. It briefly came back: reviewers were startled to find it trading again in late 2021 on shortened weekday-only hours (06:30–14:00), and the last visits recorded on Tabelog are from February 2022. Tabelog now carries the listing under a 【閉店】 heading and no source of any kind shows it trading after early 2022. A separate business, 「明神そば きやり 御茶ノ水ソラシティ店」, also closed — on 31 December 2022 — so there is no surviving Myōjin Soba in Ochanomizu under either operator.
chef_bio.specialty: 「明神そば」 ¥500 — the loaded house bowl.

anecdotes.text: Two entrances, each with its own ticket machine, so a rushing commuter never had to cross the shop.
Its closure on 2020-07-20, alongside そば新 at the Hijiribashi exit, was described by regulars as the end of standing-soba culture at Ochanomizu.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13056672 is filed under 【閉店】 with the address 神田駿河台2-6-1 御茶ノ水山水ビル1F, standing-only seating and last-published hours of 06:30–14:00 Mon–Fri. Its review timeline documents the arc precisely: closure 2020-07-20, a surprise reopening noticed in Nov–Dec 2021, and no visits after February 2022. A 2017 food blog records the pre-closure hours (6:30–20:00, Sat to 15:00), the two-door layout and the ¥500/¥280 pricing. A separate operator notice records that 明神そば きやり 御茶ノ水ソラシティ店 closed on 2022-12-31.

cultural_comfort.note: Do not send anyone here. The unit at 神田駿河台2-6-1 no longer houses Myōjin Soba. If a user wants standing soba or a cheap early breakfast at Ochanomizu, the nearest live equivalent in this dataset is しんぱち食堂 御茶ノ水店, 30 m away at 神田駿河台2-6-10, open from 06:00.

name: しんぱち食堂 御茶ノ水店
address_ja: 〒101-0062 東京都千代田区神田駿河台2-6-10 田中ビル
cuisine: Charcoal-grilled dried-fish set meals from 06:00 to 23:30, thirty-one metres from Ochanomizu station — twenty-plus fish by provenance, rice, miso soup and pickles from about ¥610, breakfast sets from ¥460
neighborhood: Kanda-Surugadai 2-chōme, 31 m from JR Ochanomizu (Chūō/Sōbu lines); Shin-Ochanomizu (Chiyoda line) and Ochanomizu (Marunouchi line) both within a few minutes
gf_detail: Promising in shape, unproven in fact — and the one allergen source that exists points the wrong way. On paper this is the safest kind of Japanese restaurant for a celiac: a salt-grilled fish, plain rice, pickles. In practice a crowd-sourced allergen table on allergy-navi.com lists 小麦 as PRESENT (〇) on every single set it covers — including plain salt-grilled salmon and sanma — which almost certainly reflects the miso soup and/or the table soy sauce and pickles rather than the fish. That table is explicitly marked 「ユーザーより提供いただいた情報で、公式情報ではありません」, so it is a warning rather than a verdict. Note also that the miso-marinade sets (西京漬け), the mirin-dried sets (みりん干し), the sake-lees sets (粕漬け) and さば味噌煮 are all seasoned, not merely salted. A celiac's realistic play is a straight 塩焼き fish plus white rice, skipping the miso soup and the table shōyu — and asking, because the chain publishes no allergen chart of its own. A blogger who eats gluten-free writes warmly about the chain for exactly this reason but is careful to say 「完全にグルテンフリーを保証するものではありません」.
vegan_detail: The entire menu is grilled fish and grilled meat; the miso soup is dashi-based; there is no plant-based set. The 60-yen side dishes include nattō and sesame-dressed green beans, which are themselves plant-based, but they are sides to a fish tray and cannot make a meal.

roles: operated by 株式会社しんぱち; acquired by すかいらーくホールディングス in March 2026
chef_bio.background: Shinpachi Shokudō's whole idea is stated plainly in its own copy: 「炭火焼干物食堂のファーストフード」 — fast food, but the fast food is charcoal-grilled dried fish. Seats are arranged in a U around a central working island so that a full washoku tray can be handed over without a wait, and the himono is cooked on a purpose-built charcoal grill the company developed to cook through in about half the usual time. The pitch to the customer is provenance and price at once: more than twenty grilled fish sourced by region, rice of the grade served in high-end ryōtei, miso soup with particular attention to dashi and miso, pickles from an old maker — sets from around ¥610, breakfast sets from ¥460, and a 60-yen add-on for a small side. Almost every branch runs from early morning to late at night, and the interiors are dressed as an Edo-period meshiya, which the company says draws a large number of overseas customers. The Ochanomizu branch opened on 22 March 2024 in the Tanaka Building thirty-one metres from the station — and, as it happens, thirty metres from the shuttered unit where the standing-soba shop 明神そば used to open at 06:30, a slot this shop now fills at 06:00. In March 2026 Skylark Holdings bought 株式会社しんぱち, previously backed by the PE firm J-STAR, for a reported ¥11 billion, with a stated plan to expand the format to 300 outlets; how that changes sourcing or menu at branch level is not yet visible.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「日本の食文化を取り戻し、進化させたい」 — recover and evolve Japanese food culture, by making a proper grilled-fish tray as fast and as cheap as a burger.
chef_bio.specialty: Charcoal-grilled himono sets — ほっけ, さば文化干し, あじ開き, サーモンハラス干し, あかうお; miso, saikyō and kasu marinades; 朝定食 from ¥460.

anecdotes.text: The counter is laid out in a U with the kitchen working in the middle, specifically so a full set meal can be handed straight across without a wait.
The chain developed its own charcoal grill that cooks himono through in roughly half the normal time.
Skylark Holdings acquired the operator in March 2026 for a reported ¥11 billion, aiming to grow the format to 300 stores.
A Japanese blogger who eats gluten-free singles the chain out as the place that rescued her from eating out — while stating clearly that it guarantees nothing.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: shinpachi-shokudo.com is the chain's own site: concept, the U-shaped counter and custom charcoal grill, the sourcing claims for rice/miso/pickles, and the full menu of fish and meat sets. Tabelog 13295457 gives the Ochanomizu branch address 神田駿河台2-6-10 田中ビル, opening date 2024-03-22, hours 06:00–23:30 with no closing day, all-non-smoking, and full card/e-money/QR acceptance. allergy-navi.com hosts a user-contributed allergen table for the chain's common menu. Nikkei and MARR Online report the March 2026 Skylark acquisition and the ¥11 billion price.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Meat sets — chicken and pork shōgayaki, beef — are cooked on the same central grill as the fish, and shōgayaki is a soy marinade.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Miso soup with every set and table soy sauce for the fish; no wheat-free soy or miso is named. Several fish are miso-, mirin- or sake-lees-marinated rather than salted.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The chain publishes no allergen chart. The only allergen data available is a user-contributed table on allergy-navi.com, which carries an explicit disclaimer that it is not official and marks 小麦 present on every set listed — including plain salt-grilled fish.

positives.text: Simple, visible cooking — a whole grilled fish, white rice, pickles — makes it far easier to reason about than a sauce-based kitchen, which is why gluten-free eaters in Japan cite the chain even without a guarantee.
Open 06:00–23:30 every day, cards, all major e-money and PayPay/d払い/楽天ペイ/au PAY accepted, non-smoking, easy to enter alone.

cultural_comfort.note: One of the easiest useful meals in central Tokyo: thirty-one metres from Ochanomizu station, open from six in the morning to half past eleven at night every day, counter seating, every card and QR method accepted, non-smoking, and comfortable to sit at alone. The chain says it gets a lot of overseas custom. Cheap — sets from about ¥610, breakfast from ¥460. Note the caveat in gf_detail before recommending it to a celiac.

roles: owner-proprietor; member house of the 満留賀 noren
chef_bio.origin: Kanda-Jimbōchō, Chiyoda-ku; the shop moved to its present address from 神田神保町1-17 in May 2007
chef_bio.background: 満留賀 is one of the old Tokyo soba noren, alongside 藪, 更科, 砂場 and 増田屋, and almost every shop carrying the name got it by noren-wake. The line starts with Katō Hōzō, who came alone to Tokyo from Hoi-gun in Aichi, apprenticed at a Mikawaya in Shitaya, and opened his own shop in Shiba Udagawachō in 1900 under the name Mikawaya with a katakana カ in a circle as his noren mark. His relatives followed him to Tokyo, his younger brother Kōzō opened in Hamamatsuchō in 1907, and the independents multiplied; by the late Meiji and early Taishō period the kanji 満留賀 had been adopted across the group, and in 1916, at twenty shops, the 満留賀会 was founded to manage the noren — later incorporated after the war as the 満留賀会麺業協同組合. Seison is the Jimbōchō member house. It sits on Suzuran-dōri among the second-hand bookshops, behind an apricot-coloured wall and a white gate, and the room inside is deliberately understated rather than decorated. The kitchen keeps a stone mill on the premises, mills its own buckwheat and hand-cuts it, and the shop's calling card is not a plain seiro but 梅肉入り揚げ蓮根そば at ¥980 — a thick round of lotus root fried in a crisp coating, ume paste for a light sourness, grated daikon to lift it, against soba the Chiyoda tourism association describes as firm enough to hold its own against the crunch. It is a lunch-and-early-evening shop for the publishing and bookselling district, open weekdays only, forty seats with a private room, capable of taking a party of fifty, and — unusually for a soba house of this vintage — it holds an English menu.
chef_bio.philosophy: A noren-wake soba house that mills and cuts its own, with one invented dish it is known for rather than a museum menu.
chef_bio.specialty: 梅肉入り揚げ蓮根そば ¥980; stone-milled, hand-cut soba; tempura.

The shop moved to its present address in May 2007 from 神田神保町1-17, a few doors away.

roles: member shop of the ちゃんのれん組合 (Chan Noren Association)
chef_bio.origin: Kanda-Jimbōchō; the parent shop is in Shinbashi. The branch opened 6 September 2024
chef_bio.background: This is a 'chan-kei' shop, and the lineage is documented by the association itself. The style begins with 神田ちえちゃんラーメン, founded under the railway viaduct at Kanda station; founding members later opened えっちゃんラーメン in Shinjuku and ひろちゃんラーメン in Ikebukuro, and the monthly study group those three ran together became, on New Year's Day 2022, the ちゃんのれん組合 — a mutual-aid body formed when the pandemic, staff shortages, ingredient inflation and a rash of imitators together threatened the style. The association now lists more than thirty member shops, runs joint purchasing and staff placement, and operates its own noodle maker, 達磨製麺. 新橋ニューともちん is one of its bigger families, with Shinbashi, Kawasaki, Kamata and this Jimbōchō branch. What arrives is a ¥750 chūka soba that a visiting reporter said could reasonably be sold as chāshū-men — thin-sliced, deeply seasoned pork covering the surface, a medium-thick flat noodle that is smooth and chewy at once, and a pork-heavy broth — plus a free bowl of white rice in small, medium or large, which is the signature courtesy of the whole chan-kei style. Ten standing places, a ticket machine at the door, cash only, and you wait at the counter for your number to be called rather than handing the ticket in. The kitchen and the return hatch are both at the far end of a narrow room, so regulars advise taking a place near the back. The branch opened on 6 September 2024 and trades essentially around the clock; the rocketnews reporter who visited in March 2025 found it busy at nine in the morning.
chef_bio.philosophy: The chan-kei bargain: a bowl loaded far beyond its price, free rice with it, standing room only, and a noren association behind it whose stated purpose is 「目指す味の維持、向上、継承」 — holding, improving and passing on the target flavour.
chef_bio.specialty: 中華そば ¥750 with free rice (small/medium/large); もり中華.

anecdotes.text: The style traces to 神田ちえちゃんラーメン under the Kanda station viaduct; the noren association was founded on New Year's Day 2022 by that shop with Shinjuku's えっちゃん and Ikebukuro's ひろちゃん, and runs its own noodle maker, 達磨製麺.
White rice is free in any of three sizes with a ¥750 bowl of ramen.

name: 神田神保町 天麩羅 はちまき
address_ja: 〒101-0051 東京都千代田区神田神保町1-19
cuisine: Edomae tempura since 1931 in a 1927 signboard-architecture building on Suzuran-dōri — the house dish is the anago-and-prawn tendon invented for Edogawa Ranpo at this counter; lunch ¥1,000–¥1,999, courses ¥5,000–¥5,999
neighborhood: Kanda-Jimbōchō 1-chōme, on Suzuran-dōri — 2–3 min from Jimbōchō (Toei Mita line, Toei Shinjuku line, Tokyo Metro Hanzōmon line)
hours_raw: 月・水・木・金・土・日・祝 11:00 - 21:00（料理L.O. 20:00／ドリンクL.O. 20:30）　火 11:00 - 20:00（火曜日はコース不可、天丼・定食のみ）　定休日：不定休

No allergen chart appears on hachimaki.jp or in any listing. The light record already had this right.

There is no vegan or vegetarian set and no accommodation is published.

chef_bio.origin: Kanda — the family business started in Suehirochō in 1907 and has been on Suzuran-dōri in Jimbōchō since 1945
chef_bio.background: The shop is named after a headband. In the Great Kantō Earthquake of 1923 Aoki Torakichi, who had just taken over the family fishmonger-caterer 魚安 in Kanda, fell into an irrigation channel while fleeing; a craftsman nearby pulled the hachimaki off his own head and hauled him out. When Torakichi opened his own place in Kanda-Toyamachō in 1931 he called it はちまき. It began as a Japanese restaurant doing fish, nimono, oden and tempura from a narrow shopfront with four or five counter seats, and became a tempura specialist because that was what customers kept coming back for. The Toyamachō shop burned in the Tokyo air raids of March 1945; Torakichi worked from a stall in Jimbōchō serving demobilised soldiers and then reopened on Suzuran-dōri later that year, in a 1927 kanban-kenchiku building — and the shop is still in that building, with the same exterior tiles as in the 1953 photograph on its history page. Jimbōchō had escaped the bombing, so for a decade it was one of the few functioning entertainment districts in Tokyo, and はちまき's upstairs room became the meeting place of the 廿七会, a circle of writers who met on the 27th of each month and later became the Tokyo Writers' Club. Edogawa Ranpo was its central figure and a pre-war regular; the anago-and-prawn tendon that is now the house dish exists because he asked Torakichi to put anago and prawn tempura on rice and pour the tare over. His calligraphy 「晝は夢 夜ぞ現」 still hangs in the room, along with signed boards from Kaionji Chōgorō and a framed gift from the playwright Hōjō Hideji; the actor Sano Shūji, from a Kanda firefighting family, was close enough to the household that they were photographed together outside the shop. Torakichi was the first chairman of the Suzuran-dōri merchants' association and pushed through its arcade in the 1960s; he fed Meiji University students and the cheer squad so freely that they came back as customers when they had jobs. His son Fumio, the third generation, left a railway job in 1959 to take over and went to Tsukiji every day for fifty years — the family story is that when he collapsed with a stroke at the market aged 78 he was still worrying about whether he could fillet the anago he had just bought. That is what brought the fourth generation, Masahiro, into the kitchen in 2009: he ran the shop through employed chefs at first, then decided to stand at the frying board himself. He runs for exercise. The line he keeps repeating in the shop's own copy is that tempura began as Edo street food for ordinary people, and that はちまき will stay a 大衆天麩羅 — a people's tempura shop — whatever the neighbourhood turns into.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「江戸前の大衆天麩羅」 — proper Edomae tempura at prices ordinary people pay, in a room that has not been modernised. The donburi tare is inherited from the second generation and adjusted daily by weather and temperature.
chef_bio.specialty: 穴子海老天丼 — the anago-and-prawn tendon created for Edogawa Ranpo; 天麩羅定食; kakiage; sesame-oil frying since 1931.

anecdotes.text: The shop is named for the headband a passing craftsman used to pull the founder out of a canal during the 1923 earthquake.

The signature anago-and-prawn tendon was invented to order for Edogawa Ranpo, who asked the second-generation owner to put anago and prawn tempura on rice and pour the tare over it. His calligraphy still hangs in the shop.

The upstairs room hosted the 廿七会, a writers' circle meeting on the 27th of every month — Edogawa Ranpo, Kaionji Chōgorō, Hōjō Hideji, Tanabe Mōichi of Kinokuniya, Ibuse Masuji — which later became the Tokyo Writers' Club.
The building dates from 1927 and the shop has been in it since 1945; the exterior tiles are the same ones visible in a photograph from around 1953.
The second-generation owner was the first chairman of the Suzuran-dōri merchants' association and drove the arcade project in the 1960s.
The third generation went to Tsukiji every morning for fifty years and, after collapsing there at 78, was reportedly still worrying about the anago he had just bought.

Tabelog 13022740 confirms the address 神田神保町1-19, the Tuesday short-hours exception, 27 seats in the main room, party capacity to 20, all-non-smoking, PayPay/Alipay accepted with cards only over ¥5,000, and the 一軒家レストラン classification.

gf_cross_contamination.text: One oil, wheat batter on every item, all day, in a room that has been frying tempura since 1931. There is no gluten-free route through the menu.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The inherited donburi tare is a soy-and-mirin reduction; no wheat-free soy is named anywhere.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Anago and prawn are the core of the kitchen and are filleted on site; vegetables go into the same oil.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergen information published. Seat-only reservations are declined for staffing reasons, though course bookings are taken by phone or through Tabelog — that is the only pre-arrival channel.

cultural_comfort.note: Walk-in for tendon and teishoku; seat-only reservations are NOT accepted (the shop says it is short-staffed), and only course bookings can be reserved, by phone (03-3291-6222) or through Tabelog. Cards only on dinner bills over ¥5,000, and at busy lunchtimes the shop may take cash or PayPay only — carry cash. On Tuesdays the kitchen does not run courses at all, only tendon and set meals, and closes an hour early. Twenty-seven to thirty-three seats in a small pre-war building, non-smoking, no dress code; lunch is genuinely cheap for what it is (¥1,000–¥1,999) while a dinner course lands around ¥5,000–¥6,000. No fixed closing day, so check the shop's X or Facebook before travelling.
